plants.name: Udupi Mallige
plants.about: Also called Shankarpura mallige, after the villages near Udupi where it is grown in home gardens. The laterite soil and humid air of this coast give it a strong scent, white colour and large flowers, which is why it carries a Geographical Indication tag. Buds open within five to six hours, so they are picked and strung before they bloom.
spec: Regular, but never standing in water. Let excess rain drain away.
Rich, well-drained laterite soil suits it best.
Organic manure through the growing months.
Wrap the flowers in banana leaf and sprinkle with water. They keep for up to 10 days, though the scent fades.
Waterlogged roots in heavy rain. Raise pots on bricks.

plants.name: Aboli
plants.about: Firecracker flower in English, Kanakambara in Kannada and Aboli in Konkani and Marathi. Its orange and coral blooms are strung into garlands across the coast.
spec: Bright morning sun, with cover from harsh afternoon sun.
Thoroughly, whenever the top few inches of soil are dry. Under-watering harms it.
Fertile, well-drained red loam, pH 6 to 7.5.
Warm and humid, 20 to 30 degrees C. It suits Mangaluru.
Liquid fertiliser every two weeks in the growing season.

plants.name: Hibiscus
plants.about: The coast's everyday flower, seen on temple offerings and garden fences. It blooms through most of the year in warm, humid weather and grows well in pots or beds.
spec: Full sun, five to six hours. It drops buds in deep shade.
When the top inch is dry. In heavy rain, let it dry between waterings.
Well-drained. Mix coarse sand into lateritic garden soil.
A light feed every two to three weeks while it flowers.
Trim leggy stems after a flush of flowers.

plants.name: Tulsi
plants.about: Holy basil, native to India and kept in a raised tulasi katte outside many coastal homes. It is a leafy herb as much as a sacred plant.
spec: Light watering, like a shower. Daily in summer, every other day in cooler weather. Do not flood the pot.
Porous, well-drained, with added organic manure.
Pinch the growing tip for a bushier plant and remove flower heads early to keep it leafy.
Mealybugs, aphids, mites and whitefly. Spray a neem-based solution.

plants.name: Curry leaf
plants.about: The kitchen tree behind every tempering. It loves warmth, so it settles in easily on the coast and needs no protection from cold.
spec: Deeply but not often. Let the top 3 to 5 cm dry between waterings to avoid root rot.
Well-drained soil that is rich in compost.
Compost or organic manure every two to three months. Nitrogen-rich feed gives lush leaves.
Pick leaves regularly from the tips so it keeps branching.

plants.name: Monstera
plants.about: The split-leaf climber that enjoys Mangaluru's humid air. It grows impressively through the monsoon months.
spec: Bright spot, away from direct afternoon sun.
Moderate. Water only when the top of the soil starts to dry.
Mix in coarse sand or perlite for drainage.
Give it airflow and watch for fungal spots in wet weather.

plants.name: Canna lily
plants.about: A sturdy flowering plant that handles the monsoon better than almost any other. A good choice for a bed that stays wet.
spec: Full sun for the most flowers.
Generous in dry spells. It copes with heavy rain.
Rich soil that drains, with compost worked in.
Cut spent flower stalks and old leaves at the base.

month: Check every pot has drainage holes, and clear the saucers after rain.
Mulch bare soil to stop splash and keep roots steady.
Give ferns and balcony plants airflow to avoid fungus.
Sow spinach, amaranth and fenugreek, which enjoy the humidity.
Shield young plants from strong wind and heavy downpours.
Mix coarse sand into laterite soil so roots do not sit wet.
